transformations.lexical: Unicode letter/apostrophe tokens; unigrams/bigrams; sublinear TF; smoothed IDF; L2 normalization; min_df=1; max_features=12000; English stop list retains no/not/nor/never.
transformations.semantic: The same complete-phrase mask, followed by the pinned model tokenizer; function words retained and every nonoverlapping 240-wordpiece chunk encoded.

model.token_pooling: Attention-mask mean including CLS/SEP, then chunk L2 normalization
model.document_pooling: Content-wordpiece-weighted mean of normalized chunks, then document L2 normalization
model.cache: No disk cache; vectors retained in memory during execution

projections.method: Lexical uncentered TruncatedSVD with two components and neural centered PCA with two components, independently fitted. Coordinates are centered and scaled to RMS radius 1.
projections.alignment: Orthogonal Procrustes rotates or reflects the displayed neural 2D points toward the lexical 2D points. This changes display orientation only; it does not align latent meanings.
projections.scope: The 2D positions are lossy visualization coordinates. Consult explained variance, neighborhood trustworthiness and full-space cosines. No belief, historical or physical geometry is inferred.

term_overlay.selection: Union of the top six mean TF-IDF features per medium, in alphabetic medium-ID order, capped at 30. Descriptive selection, not independently tested markers.
term_overlay.scope: Mean L2-normalized document TF-IDF weights per source context. These lexical feature vectors are not neural word embeddings. Exact printed phrases are masked, but unlisted name variants remain; words such as arcturian and council can retain identity information.

topics.selection: Three fixed exploratory display factors; not an optimized or validated doctrine count.

lexical.selection: Three fixed exploratory display clusters; not selected as optimal or validated doctrine categories.

semantic.algorithm: KMeans on L2-normalized document representations, n_init=10.

synthetic_controls.scope: Five constructed stress-case statements, not observed channeling passages or an accuracy benchmark. A high cosine can coexist with opposite polarity or changed conditional scope.

hypotheses.question: Does language proximity track medium more than shared comparison labels?
hypotheses.operationalization: Inspect dependent pair means and cluster adjusted Rand indices against medium and comparison labels; there is no identified causal contrast.
hypotheses.limitation: The six-medium frame is unequal, several labels occur in only one medium, and written/ASR formats and dates are mixed.

hypotheses.question: Do lexical and neural representations retrieve the same neighboring source editions?
hypotheses.operationalization: Top-five neighbor-set Jaccard and the rank correlation of all 300 pairs, using fixed source IDs.
hypotheses.limitation: Neighbor agreement is representation consistency, not answer accuracy.

hypotheses.question: Do length, identity wording and chunk pooling change the neighborhood?
hypotheses.operationalization: Whole text versus a centered 300-token span; masked versus unmasked names; weighted versus equal chunk pooling.
hypotheses.limitation: Centered spans are not random or representative excerpts; length cannot be isolated causally from content.

hypotheses.question: Can a high neural similarity coexist with negation or conditional scope?
hypotheses.operationalization: Five constructed statements, kept separate from the 25 observed source editions.
hypotheses.limitation: One illustrative negation/condition stress case; no measured contradiction-detection accuracy.

limitations: Purposive English accessible-source editions, not a representative sample of religions, all channels or authenticated beings.
All 25 text editions reuse previously retained material; overlapping older frame counts cannot be added as new observations.
Four ASRs have unknown utterance roles and unmeasured recognition accuracy. A full mixed interview is not pure Council speech.
Written and machine-text formats, medium, date, length and shared vocabulary are confounded.
Pair observations are dependent. Descriptive means and exploratory clusters do not establish significance or probabilities.
Broad civilization comparisons and identical printed personality names are different source claims; neither verifies identity or independent origin.
Pinned MiniLM is a lightweight reproducible baseline, not a current SOTA claim. No new weights or neural word embeddings are trained.
Only complete listed name phrases are masked. Unlisted aliases, shortened names, inflections and contextual identity cues remain.
Cosines, coordinates and nearest neighbors are not common answers or contradictions; source-reading questions and cards form that separate layer.
The five constructed control statements are explicitly synthetic and excluded from corpus and reading denominators.
